clue.text: Bill and Cyril worked to produce fibre

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

indicators.note: worked means the name Cyril is kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: Two colleagues, Bill and Cyril, labour together to manufacture textile fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name beside Cyril, but it is an account, AC. 'worked' rearranges CYRIL into RYLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic textile fibre used in knitwear and fabrics.

clue.text: Grants permits

definitions.meaning: grants as a verb: gives or concedes
permits as a verb: lets happen

explanation.surface: Two near-synonyms side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs meaning to let someone have or do something, a straight synonym each way.

clue.text: Distant meteor disintegrates

indicators.note: a meteor that disintegrates breaks apart, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A faraway meteor breaks up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remote is far away, a straight synonym for distant.

clue.text: No choice for this holiday destination?

definitions.text: No choice for this holiday destination?

parts.words: No choice for this holiday destination?
parts.note: the phrase for what you fall back on when nothing else is possible, read as the final seaside place you might go on holiday

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker is stuck going somewhere they never chose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an option taken only because nothing else remains, punning on a holiday resort.

clue.text: Canine tooth one has right in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre means the right goes into the middle of the tooth-and-one pair

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dog's canine tooth is described, as if a dentist were explaining its position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as the tooth but is the definition: a dog. 'in the centre' places R in the middle of COGI.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged breed of dog, so an example of a canine.

clue.text: Wages and gratuity in post

indicators.note: in tells us the gratuity sits inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a gratuity is a tip

explanation.surface: An employee's pay package includes salary plus a tip in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job or the mail itself, but is the verb: to send. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, a kind of salary or wages, especially for clergy or students.

clue.text: You may wind up eating it

definitions.text: You may wind up eating it

parts.words: You may wind up eating it
parts.note: wind up suggests ending up, but literally you twirl these long strands around a fork before eating

explanation.surface: A wry warning that you may end up eating something.
explanation.definitionFit: The long pasta strands are twirled round a fork, literally wound up, when eaten.

clue.text: Girl puts one over teacher being sent up

indicators.note: over places the one above the next piece in this down answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: being sent up means the word is read upwards, reversed in a down clue

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl gets one over on a teacher who is being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' suggests mockery but reverses SIR to RIS, placed under I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Split up and set off with compass

indicators.note: off means the word set is thrown out of order

parts.note: compass as a noun means scope or range

explanation.surface: A couple separate and head off, guided by a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into EST, and 'compass' is range or scope, not the navigational device.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to drive apart people who were close, causing a split or separation.

clue.text: Give one an order to paint?

definitions.meaning: to honour someone with a medal or order of chivalry
to paint and paper a room

explanation.surface: Someone is told to start painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an order' looks like an instruction but means an honour such as a knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both awarding a medal and doing up a room with paint.

clue.text: Fifty-one doctors appear to be members

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree; MBS is the plural

explanation.surface: Fifty-one doctors turn up to a meeting as members.
explanation.definitionFit: Members in the old sense are parts of the body, arms and legs.

clue.text: Article is made true to life

indicators.note: made means the letters of article is are reconstructed

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is written to be faithful to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction that is lifelike or accurate in representing reality is called realistic.

clue.text: Certain to get drunk on Adam's ale

indicators.note: on in an across clue means following the other piece

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular name for water, the only drink Adam had
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to get drunk, though only on water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's ale' is old slang for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A watertight case or argument is unassailable, so certain.

clue.text: Look on pound as an animal refuge

indicators.note: on means the look comes after the pound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra
an air is a manner or look, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a dog pound as a refuge for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests an animal enclosure but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild beast's den or hiding place is called its lair.

clue.text: Powerless person in the air

parts.note: powerless suggests helplessness, but here means flying without an engine, gliding beneath a wing

explanation.surface: Someone is helplessly floating high up.
explanation.definitionFit: This sport's pilot flies an unpowered wing, so is literally without power while airborne.

clue.text: Sounds like narrow waters but don't be confused

indicators.note: sounds like says we hear the phrase rather than read it

parts.note: a sea strait is a narrow channel of water

explanation.surface: A geography quiz: a narrow channel, but don't mix it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' also hints at a sound, a strait of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive clearly and think clearly is the opposite of being muddled.

clue.text: They may pass on what they know

definitions.text: They may pass on what they know

parts.words: They may pass on what they know
parts.note: pass on suggests teaching others, but means getting through a test thanks to their knowledge

explanation.surface: Teachers who hand on their knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates sitting a test pass on the strength of what they know.

clue.text: Take-away Chinese place?

definitions.meaning: to carry someone off by force, especially to crew a ship
the great port city in China

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal from a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-away' reads as a Chinese meal but is the verb meaning to kidnap.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to press-gang or kidnap, and the city is China's largest port.

clue.text: Summary is merely theoretical

definitions.meaning: a brief précis of a paper
existing in thought rather than concrete form

explanation.surface: A précis is dismissed as merely theory.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a précis of a paper; the adjective means conceptual rather than concrete.

clue.text: Breathing in irregularly when asleep in winter

indicators.note: irregularly means the letters of breathing in are put in a disordered sequence

explanation.surface: A sleeper breathes unevenly through the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that pass the cold season in a dormant state, like bears and hedgehogs, are doing this.

clue.text: Be up in time for a parliamentary occasion

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: An MP is up in time for a session of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be up' reads as being out of bed, but 'up' is a reversal signal in a down entry; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal discussion in the Commons, where motions are argued and voted on, is a debate.

clue.text: Beauty that totally occupies the viewer

definitions.meaning: literally an organ of sight that is completely full

explanation.surface: A beautiful sight fills the onlooker's gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a striking person or sight, and literally as much as the organ of sight can hold.

clue.text: Stagger back, deprived of one's wits

indicators.note: back means the word for stagger is read from right to left

parts.note: to stagger someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Someone reels back, out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' looks like reeling but means astonish, STUN, reversed by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crazy or mad is a colloquial sense of the word, so having lost one's reason.

clue.text: It raises the spirit

parts.note: raises the spirit suggests cheering someone up, but means producing whisky or gin

explanation.surface: Something uplifting that lifts one's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where whisky and other strong liquor is produced, so it brings spirits into being.

clue.text: Get child out of bed to do sums

parts.note: a tot is a small child
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: A parent rouses a child to do homework sums.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to add numbers together to reach a total.

clue.text: Stop! It's a hold-up!

definitions.meaning: to staunch or halt a flow, as of blood
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A cry from a robbery: stop, it's a hold-up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' sounds like a robbery but means a stalk that supports a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to halt a flow; the noun is a plant's supporting stalk.

clue.text: Courage perceived to be genuine

parts.note: heart means courage, as in take heart
felt means sensed or perceived

explanation.surface: Bravery that is felt is shown to be real.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are sincere and deeply felt are called heartfelt.

clue.text: Overshadow Snow White's friend

definitions.meaning: to make something seem small by comparison
one of the seven little companions in the fairy tale

explanation.surface: Someone eclipses one of Snow White's companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to dwarf by comparison; Snow White had seven small companions like Grumpy.

clue.text: This difficult sum recalled Panama, perhaps

indicators.note: difficult means the word this is put into a tricky, scrambled order
recalled means the word sum is called back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A tricky sum from school is remembered alongside Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges THIS into ISTH, and 'recalled' reverses SUM to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a narrow strip of land joining two larger landmasses, an example of this landform.

clue.text: Cruel fluctuation in pence and pound for composer

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word between the two money abbreviations

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling

indicators.note: fluctuation means the letters of cruel shift into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Harsh swings in the value of the pound and pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuation' gives URCEL, and 'in' sits it between the money abbreviations; 'pound' is L from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was an English Baroque composer, writer of Dido and Aeneas.
